rationale:
One event for four view changes landing together as a batch, because the watch contract admits a single event per capability family per change set and each of the four authored its own while it was a standalone PR. The individual rationales are preserved verbatim below, each under the branch that wrote it; nothing is summarised away.

--- 20260912-widget-bridge-child-ordering-watch ---
Record a Pulp-owned correctness fix in how the widget bridge orders a parent's children. Every native createX call appends, and nothing on the bridge could position an existing child, so the rendered order was the order widgets happened to reach the bridge rather than the order their author wrote. The renderer already knew better: host-config's attach() computed an insert index and kept childIds and the DOM shim in that order, then discarded the index at materialize(), and its insertBefore() reorder branch probed for insertChild and moveWidget, neither of which any native host defined. The observable failure is a subtree that mounts into a parent which kept its other children -- a re-opened dropdown remounts its rows after the siblings that stayed, so captions separate from the descriptions they label. This adds insertChild(parentId, childId, index), which repositions a widget that already exists, backed by View::move_child_to_index. It is purely additive: no existing bridge signature changes, and a renderer bundle running against an older host still mounts, appending exactly as before. It is a reorder and never a reparent -- a parentId that does not own the named child fails closed rather than restructuring the tree -- and reordering does not run the attach/detach lifecycle, so a moved subtree keeps its focus, drag and popup state. Child order is an input to layout and paint, so a rendered tree changes only where it was already wrong; no design ingest, captured output, packaging boundary, accepted expansion boundary, or Vellum source authority is affected.

--- 20260912-popup-active-highlight-deferred-watch ---
An opened dropdown lit two rows: the app's own selected row plus the web-compat popup owner's keyboard cursor, painted before any pointer or key input. The cursor is now created but not painted until the user reveals it by hovering a row, pressing an arrow, or opening the popup with an arrow, and the first arrow steps off an ARIA-selected seed while landing on an edge seed. render-assets-and-backends is crossed only because core/view/js/web-compat-document.js sits under that family's selector; the diff changes when one inline background is assigned and which index an arrow key computes, inside one popup-ownership IIFE. No renderer, backend, Skia pin, asset, font, shader, surface, harness, fixture, snapshot or threshold changes, and no bridge function, manifest row or generated artifact. Registered watch-only so the family's coverage stays honest about a change that crossed its selector. No authority moves and no Vellum artifact changes.

--- 20260912-overlay-dismissal-single-policy-watch ---
Crosses the render-assets-and-backends watch family only through its broad `core/view/**` selector. Every file in this change is under core/view: the new core/view/include/pulp/view/overlay_dismissal.hpp and core/view/src/overlay_dismissal.cpp, the two platform macOS hosts, the Windows plugin input router header, the web event-translation header, pointer_dispatch.{hpp,cpp}, and the view source manifest. Nothing under core/canvas or core/render is touched, no Skia, Dawn, or render-backend selector is crossed, no design-system asset changes, and no packaging or asset-resolution behaviour changes. The change consolidates four hand-rolled copies of the overlay-dismissal policy into one implementation the platform hosts call: route_press_to_active_overlay and route_context_press move unchanged out of pointer_dispatch.cpp, route_escape_to_active_overlay is added and carries the Escape ordering the standalone macOS host previously spelled out inline, and root_overlay_owns_keyboard answers a deliberately narrower question without acting, so a plugin host can decide whether to hold the DAW keyboard. The behavioural deltas are that the standalone and web hosts now read the root-owned overlay slot instead of the process-global shim mirror, the web host routes a press into the overlay's own subtree and honours outside-click consumption, both DAW plugin hosts gain an Escape path they did not have, and the standalone host's right button moves onto the overlay-aware context-press verb it had never consulted. No rendering, paint, layout, or asset behaviour changes, no accepted expansion boundary moves, and no Vellum source authority changes.
